(Fort Smith, Arkansas) | college = [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]] (2018–2020) | highlights = * [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] All-Freshman team (2019) | medal_templates = }} '''Isaiah Joe''' (born July 2, 1999) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas Razorbacks]]. ==Early life and high school career== Joe grew up in [[Fort Smith, Arkansas]] and attended [[Northside High School (Fort Smith, Arkansas)|Northside High School]].{{cite web|url=https://www.vanburencountydem.com/sports/20190313/ua-basketball-everyday-joe-ignites-hogs?template=ampart|title=UA Basketball: 'Everyday Joe' ignites Hogs|work=Van Buren County Democrat|date=March 13, 2019|access-date=November 13, 2019}} He shot 41% from three-point range in his sophomore season and committed to play [[college basketball]] at the [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|University of Arkansas]] during the summer going into his junior year over offers from [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]] and [[Little Rock Trojans men's basketball|Arkansas-Little Rock]].{{cite web|url=https://www.arkansasfight.com/2016/8/2/12364674/arkansas-basketball-recruiting-isaiah-joe-commits-razorbacks|title=Arkansas Basketball Recruiting: Isaiah Joe Commits to the Razorbacks|first=Doc|last=Harper|website=ArkansasFight.com|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|date=August 2, 2016|access-date=November 13, 2019}} As a junior, Joe averaged 18.8 points, 4.5 rebounds and 2.2 steals per game and helped lead the Grizzlies to an [[Arkansas Activities Association]] (AAA) 7A state championship and was named first team All-State.{{cite web|url=https://5newsonline.com/2017/11/08/northsides-isaiah-joe-signs-with-razorbacks/|title=Northside’s Isaiah Joe Signs With Razorbacks|first=Brooke|last=Grimsley|website=[[KFSM-TV|5NewsOnline.com]]|date=November 8, 2017|access-date=November 13, 2019}} As a senior, Joe averaged 22.8 points, 4.4 rebounds, 3.4 assists and 2.9 steals per game and was named the Gatorade Arkansas Boys Basketball Player of the Year and the State Player of the Year by ''[[USA Today]]'' as he led Northside to the state title game before eventually falling to [[North Little Rock High School]].{{cite web|url=https://www.swtimes.com/sports/20180309/basketball-northsides-joe-named-gatorade-player-of-year|title=Basketball: Northside’s Joe named Gatorade Player of the Year|first=Buck|last=Ringgold|work=[[Southwest Times Record]]|date=March 9, 2018|access-date=November 13, 2019}}{{cite web|url=https://usatodayhss.com/2018/2017-18-all-usa-arkansas-boys-basketball-team|title=2017-18 ALL-USA Arkansas Boys Basketball Team|first=Evan|last=Hilbert|website=[[USA Today|USATodayHSS.com]]|date=April 16, 2018|access-date=November 13, 2019}} ==College career== Joe averaged 13.9 points, 2.8 rebounds, 1.7 assists and 1.5 steals per game over 34 games played as a freshman and was named to the [[Southeastern Conference]] (SEC) All-Freshman team.{{cite web|url=https://www.kait8.com/2019/03/13/arkansas-guard-isaiah-joe-named-sec-all-freshman-team/|title=Arkansas guard Isaiah Joe named to SEC All-Freshman Team|website=[[KAIT|KAIT.com]]|date=March 12, 2019|access-date=November 13, 2019}} He made 113 [[three-pointer]]s on 273 attempts (41.4%), breaking the Arkansas record previously held by [[Scotty Thurman]] (102) and tying the record for a freshman in the SEC while also leading the conference in three-point percentage.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/arkansas/Article/Isaiah-Joe-Arkansas-Razorbacks-playmaking-ability-Red-White-Game-136611366/|title=Isaiah Joe displays playmaking ability|first=Pete|last=Roulier|date=October 6, 2019|access-date=November 13, 2019}}{{cite news|url=https://www.swtimes.com/sports/20191007/steady-joe-impresses-new-coach|title=Steady Joe impresses new coach|work=[[Southwest Times Record]]|date=October 7, 2019|access-date=November 13, 2019}} He was also named the SEC Player of the Week after scoring 34 points on 10 of 13 shooting from three (11–14 overall) against [[2018–19 FIU Panthers men's basketball team|FIU]] on December 1, 2018.{{cite web|url=https://www.4029tv.com/article/isaiah-joe-earns-sec-player-of-the-week-honor/25384179|title=Isaiah Joe earns SEC Player of the Week honor|first=Jourdan|last=Black|website=[[KHBS|4029TV.com]]|date=December 3, 2018|access-date=November 13, 2019}} Entering his sophomore season, Joe was named preseason All-SEC and to [[Jerry West Award]] watchlist.{{cite news|url=https://www.nwaonline.com/news/2019/nov/05/isaiah-joe-makes-coaches-preseason-all-/|title=Isaiah Joe makes coaches' preseason all-SEC team|work=[[Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]]|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|date=November 5, 2019|access-date=November 13, 2019}}{{cite web|url=https://razorbackers.com/2019/10/16/razorback-basketball-isaiah-joe-named-to-jerry-west-award-watch-list/|title=Razorback Basketball: Isaiah Joe named to Jerry West Award Watch List|first=Easton|last=Leonard|website=RazorBackers.com|publisher=[[FanSided]]}} Joe was also named the 80th-best collegiate basketball player going into the 2019–20 season by ''[[CBS Sports]]'' and the 33rd-best prospect for the [[2020 NBA draft]] by ''[[ESPN]]''.{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/ranking-the-top-100-and-1-best-players-in-college-basketball-entering-the-2019-20-season/|title=Ranking the Top 100 And 1 best players in college basketball entering the 2019-20 season|first1=Kyle|last1=Boone|first2=Matt|last2=Norlander|first3=Gary|last3=Parrish|website=CBSSports.com|date=October 24, 2019|access-date=November 13, 2019}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/insider/story/_/id/27998169/nba-mock-draft-viewer-guide-our-top-prospects|title=NBA mock draft: Viewer's guide for our top prospects|first=Jonathan|last=Givony|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=November 4, 2019|access-date=November 13, 2019}} Joe was named the SEC co-Player of the Week on January 2, 2020, following a 24 point, five rebound performance in a 71–64 win against [[2019–20 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|Indiana]].{{cite web|url=https://www.thv11.com/article/sports/isaiah-joe-named-sec-co-player-of-the-week/91-f1135f0c-a18b-4972-b98d-86db46970215|title=Isaiah Joe named SEC Co-Player of the Week|website=[[KTHV|THV11.com]]|date=December 30, 2019|access-date=January 2, 2020}} Joe scored 34 points, including 26 in the second half, on January 12 to lead Arkansas in a 76–72 comeback win over [[2019–20 Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball team|Ole Miss]].{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/arkansas/Article/Isaiah-Joe-Arkansas-Razorbacks-Ole-Miss-Rebels--142084524/|title=Isaiah Joe wills Razorbacks to victory over Rebels|first=Pete|last=Rouler|website=247Sports.com|date=January 12, 2020|access-date=January 17, 2020}} On February 4, Joe underwent an arthroscopic procedure on his knee after an MRI revealed inflammation and was ruled out indefinitely.{{cite news |last1=Boone |first1=Kyle |title=Arkansas star Isaiah Joe, a potential first-round NBA Draft pick, out indefinitely after knee surgery |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/arkansas-star-isaiah-joe-a-potential-first-round-nba-draft-pick-out-indefinitely-after-knee-surgery/ |accessdate=February 5, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=February 4, 2020}} As a sophomore, Joe averaged 16.9 points and 4.1 rebounds per game.{{cite news |last1=Roulier |first1=Pete |title=Joe lands low on ESPN's draft board |url=https://247sports.com/college/arkansas/Article/Isaiah-Joe-NBA-Draft-ESPN-mock--145900259/ |accessdate=April 14, 2020 |work=247 Sports |date=April 10, 2020}} Following the season he declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]].{{cite news |title=Arkansas’ Isaiah Joe declares for 2020 NBA draft |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2020/04/20/arkansas-isaiah-joe-declares-for-2020-nba-draft/ |accessdate=April 21, 2020 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=April 20, 2020}} On August 1, Joe announced he was withdrawing from the draft and returning to Arkansas.{{cite news |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |title=Isaiah Joe withdraws from NBA draft, returning to Arkansas |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29578413/isaiah-joe-withdraws-draft-returning-arkansas |accessdate=August 2, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=August 1, 2020}} However, on August 17 he reversed course and left Arkansas for the professional ranks.{{cite news |last1=Boone |first1=Kyle |title=2020 NBA Draft: Arkansas standout Isaiah Joe reverses course, re-enters draft |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/2020-nba-draft-arkansas-standout-isaiah-joe-reverses-course-re-enters-draft/ |accessdate=October 23, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=August 17,
